chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Mu'awiyah ibn Hakim, who said:

I asked Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام: “At what time is it more beloved to you that we depart from Jam'?” He said: “A little before the sun rises; that is the most beloved of times to me.” I said: “If we remain until the sun rises?” He said: “There is no harm in it.”

key_terms.أَبَا إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Abū Ibrāhīm, the Imam addressed in the narration
key_terms.أَحَبُّ السَّاعَاتِ: the most beloved time, indicating recommendation
key_terms.جَمْعٍ: Jam', referring to al-Muzdalifah in the hajj rites
key_terms.قَبْلَ أَنْ تَطْلُعَ الشَّمْسُ: shortly before sunrise, the preferred time mentioned
key_terms.لَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ: there is no harm in it, indicating permissibility
key_terms.نُفِيضَ: that we depart or proceed onward in ritual movement

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended time to depart from Jam' during hajj, and is staying until sunrise allowed?
ai.summary: This hadith states the preferred time for departing from Jam' is shortly before sunrise. It also clarifies that remaining there until sunrise is permissible and involves no harm, indicating a recommendation rather than an obligation.
